## 1. Purpose

This SOP describes the fluorometric microplate method for measuring the
potential activity of extracellular enzymes in soils. Extracellular
enzymes mediate the decomposition of organic matter and the cycling of
carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur in soils. Assays use
fluorogenic substrates based on 4-methylumbelliferone (MUB) and
7-amino-4-methylcoumarin (AMC), which release a fluorescent product
upon enzymatic hydrolysis [@sinsabaugh1994; @german2011; @bell2013].
The method is high-throughput (96-well microplate format), sensitive,
and widely used in soil biogeochemistry and ecosystem ecology.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Measurement of potential hydrolytic enzyme activities
  in field-moist, sieved (less than 2 mm) mineral and organic soils
  from EA Program sites, using MUB- and AMC-linked fluorogenic
  substrates in a 96-well microplate format
- **Does not apply to:** Oxidative enzyme assays (e.g., phenol oxidase,
  peroxidase), which use colorimetric substrates (L-DOPA); enzyme
  assays in aquatic samples (requires modified dilution); commercially
  available enzyme activity kits with different substrates
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Lab Manager  | Select target enzymes; approve substrate concentrations |
| Trained Personnel | Prepare reagents, run assays, analyze data              |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** MUB and AMC substrates are dissolved in dimethyl
  sulfoxide (DMSO), which is readily absorbed through the skin and can
  carry dissolved solutes into the body. Sodium acetate buffer and
  sodium hydroxide (for pH adjustment) are mild to moderate irritants.
  Concentrated NaOH is corrosive.
- **Biological:** Soil samples may contain pathogens. Handle with
  gloves.
- **Physical:** Microplate reader UV lamp may cause eye strain with
  prolonged direct viewing.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (double glove when handling DMSO solutions)

### Emergency Procedures

For DMSO contact with skin, wash immediately with soap and water (do
not use ethanol, which enhances absorption). For NaOH contact, flush
with water for 15 minutes. Refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd).

## 6. Target Enzymes and Substrates

The following enzymes are routinely assayed in the EA Program. Other
MUB- or AMC-linked substrates can be added using the same general
protocol.

| Enzyme                        | Abbreviation | Substrate                                    | Nutrient Cycle | Substrate Conc. |
|:------------------------------|:-------------|:---------------------------------------------|:---------------|:----------------|
| $\beta$-1,4-glucosidase       | BG           | 4-MUB-$\beta$-D-glucopyranoside              | Carbon         | 200 $\mu$M      |
| Cellobiohydrolase             | CBH          | 4-MUB-$\beta$-D-cellobioside                 | Carbon         | 200 $\mu$M      |
| $\beta$-1,4-N-acetylglucosaminidase | NAG   | 4-MUB-N-acetyl-$\beta$-D-glucosaminide       | Carbon / Nitrogen | 200 $\mu$M   |
| Acid (alkaline) phosphatase   | AP           | 4-MUB-phosphate                              | Phosphorus     | 200 $\mu$M      |
| $\beta$-1,4-xylosidase        | BX           | 4-MUB-$\beta$-D-xylopyranoside               | Carbon         | 200 $\mu$M      |
| Leucine aminopeptidase        | LAP          | L-Leucine-7-AMC                              | Nitrogen       | 200 $\mu$M      |
| Sulfatase                     | SUL          | 4-MUB-sulfate                                | Sulfur         | 200 $\mu$M      |

: Target enzymes, substrates, and associated nutrient cycles. {#tbl-enzymes}


## 7. Procedure

### 7.1 Soil Slurry Preparation

1. Weigh 1.0 g of field-moist, sieved (less than 2 mm) soil into a
   clean container.
2. Add 125 mL of 50 mM sodium acetate buffer (pH adjusted to match
   the soil pH, typically 5.0 for acidic soils or 7.8 for alkaline
   soils) [@german2011].
3. Homogenize with a magnetic stir bar or by vortexing for 1 minute.
4. Keep the slurry stirring continuously during pipetting to maintain
   a uniform suspension.

### 7.2 Substrate Stock Preparation

1. Dissolve each MUB or AMC substrate in DMSO to prepare a 10 mM
   stock solution. Store at --20 °C in amber vials; stable for at
   least 6 months.
2. Prepare working solutions by diluting the DMSO stock in buffer to
   the target concentration (typically 200 $\mu$M final concentration
   in the well).
3. Prepare MUB and AMC calibration standards in buffer at
   concentrations of 0, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, 10, and 25 $\mu$M.

### 7.3 Microplate Layout

For each soil sample, set up the following wells (8 analytical
replicates per enzyme) [@bell2013]:

| Well Type              | Contents                                       | Purpose              |
|:-----------------------|:-----------------------------------------------|:---------------------|
| Sample assay (n = 8)   | 200 $\mu$L slurry + 50 $\mu$L substrate        | Enzyme activity      |
| Sample control (n = 8) | 200 $\mu$L slurry + 50 $\mu$L buffer            | Soil background fluorescence |
| Substrate control (n = 8) | 200 $\mu$L buffer + 50 $\mu$L substrate      | Substrate autofluorescence |
| MUB/AMC standard curve | 200 $\mu$L buffer + 50 $\mu$L standard          | Calibration          |
| Blank                  | 200 $\mu$L buffer + 50 $\mu$L buffer             | Instrument blank     |

### 7.4 Incubation

1. Seal the plate with an adhesive seal.
2. Incubate at 20 °C (or field-relevant temperature) in the dark on
   a plate shaker at low speed for 2--4 hours. The incubation time
   depends on expected activity; 3 hours is a standard starting point
   [@sinsabaugh1994].

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
For soils with unknown activity, run a pilot plate at 1, 2, and
4 hours to identify the linear range. Activity calculations assume
linearity over the incubation period; if the reaction plateaus, shorten
the incubation.
:::

### 7.5 Stopping and Reading

1. After incubation, add 10 $\mu$L of 1 N NaOH to each well to stop
   the reaction and maximize fluorescence of the MUB/AMC product
   (the fluorophore is brightest above pH 10).
2. Read fluorescence on the microplate reader at excitation 365 nm /
   emission 450 nm within 5 minutes of adding NaOH.
3. Export the raw fluorescence data for analysis.


## 8. Data Analysis and Calculations

### 8.1 Activity Calculation

For each enzyme, calculate the net fluorescence:

$$
F_{\text{net}} = F_{\text{sample}} - F_{\text{soil control}} - F_{\text{substrate control}} + F_{\text{blank}}
$$

Convert net fluorescence to nmol of product released using the MUB or
AMC standard curve (linear regression of fluorescence vs.
concentration).

Calculate enzyme activity:

$$
\text{Activity} \; (\text{nmol g}^{-1} \text{h}^{-1}) =
\frac{F_{\text{net}} / m \times V_{\text{well}}}{M_{\text{soil}} \times t}
$$

where $m$ = slope of the standard curve (fluorescence per nmol),
$V_{\text{well}}$ = total well volume (L), $M_{\text{soil}}$ = dry
mass equivalent of soil in the well (g, corrected for moisture
content per [SOP-L400](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd)), and $t$ =
incubation time (h).

```{r}
#| label: enzyme-activity-calc
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# Example enzyme activity calculation
library(tidyverse)

# Standard curve data
standards <- tibble(
  conc_uM = c(0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.5, 5.0, 10.0, 25.0),
  fluorescence = c(120, 850, 1580, 3750, 7200, 14100, 34500)
)

# Fit linear model
cal_model <- lm(fluorescence ~ conc_uM, data = standards)
slope <- coef(cal_model)[2]  # fluorescence units per uM

# Sample data (means of 8 replicates)
F_sample <- 5200
F_soil_ctrl <- 350
F_sub_ctrl <- 180
F_blank <- 125

F_net <- F_sample - F_soil_ctrl - F_sub_ctrl + F_blank

# Convert to concentration (uM in well)
conc_well <- F_net / slope

# Calculate activity
V_well_L <- 250e-6          # 250 uL total well volume in liters
soil_fresh_g <- 1.0         # g fresh soil in 125 mL slurry
frac_in_well <- 200 / (125 * 1000)  # fraction of slurry in well
soil_in_well_g <- soil_fresh_g * frac_in_well
moisture <- 0.25            # gravimetric moisture content
soil_dry_g <- soil_in_well_g * (1 - moisture)
incubation_h <- 3

activity <- (conc_well * V_well_L * 1e6) / (soil_dry_g * incubation_h)
# Result in nmol / g dry soil / h

cat(sprintf("Net fluorescence: %.0f\n", F_net))
cat(sprintf("Activity: %.1f nmol g-1 h-1\n", activity))
```


## 9. Quality Control

- Run 8 analytical replicates per enzyme per sample. Report the mean
  and coefficient of variation; CV should be less than 20%.
- Include substrate and soil quench controls on every plate.
- Run the MUB/AMC standard curve on each plate (do not carry over
  calibrations between plates, as reader sensitivity may drift).
- Include a laboratory reference soil in each batch to track
  inter-batch variability.
- Verify that activity is linear over the incubation period by running
  a time-course pilot for new soil types.


## 10. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Plate contents (soil slurry + substrates) | Drain with copious water (dilute, non-hazardous at assay concentrations) |
| DMSO substrate stock waste    | Collect in organic waste; EH&S pickup    |
| NaOH waste                    | Neutralize and drain                     |
| Used microplates              | Standard trash                           |
| Used pipette tips              | Standard trash                          |

## 13. Training Record

Before performing soil enzyme assays independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Review the SDS for DMSO, NaOH, and the fluorogenic substrates
4. Observe a trained operator perform a complete assay (slurry
   preparation through plate reading and data export)
5. Perform the assay under supervision with acceptable QC results
   (replicate CV less than 20%; standard curve $r^2 > 0.99$)
6. Demonstrate correct use of the multichannel pipette and microplate
   reader
7. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
